definition: The volume of an olive — a standard halachic measure for how much food must be eaten to trigger certain blessings or obligations.
Objects set aside by their nature or designated use as unfit to be handled on Shabbat or Yom Tov.
A symbolic enclosure, typically of wire strung between poles, that permits carrying items in an otherwise public domain on Shabbat.
Leavened grain product, forbidden to own, eat, or benefit from during Pesach.
The fringes tied to the corners of a four-cornered garment, commanded in Numbers 15:38.
The body of Jewish dietary law governing which foods may be eaten and how they must be prepared.
accepted communal custom.
practical Jewish law.
Rabbinic decisors whose rulings determine practical halacha for a question or community.
a divine commandment.
blessing.
The ceremony, with wine, spices, and a braided candle, marking the end of Shabbat or a festival.
A halachically defined point or window of time in the day (e.g., sunrise, sunset, the latest time for the morning Shema).
A procedure performed before a Yom Tov that falls on a Friday, permitting food preparation on the holiday for Shabbat.
A stringency a person or community adopts beyond the strict letter of the law.
A halachically valid leniency, as opposed to a chumra (stringency).
The specific liturgical text and order of prayer a community follows (e.g., Nusach Ashkenaz, Nusach Sefard).
Ritual immersion in a mikveh (or other qualifying body of water) for purposes of ritual purity.
A formal Jewish bill of divorce, required to dissolve a Jewish marriage.
A halachic question posed to a rabbi — the origin of this project's name.
